recommendations: Add NVIDIA Difix3D+ as an optional Colab post-training pass: render frames along an interpolated fly-through path through the gsplat/Brush scene, clean them with the nvidia/difix or nvidia/difix_ref checkpoint (single-step SD-Turbo-scale diffusion, the lightest model in this cluster), then feed the cleaned frames back as extra pseudo-GT for a short gsplat/Brush re-optimization. This is the only method in the cluster with public weights, a documented nerfstudio/gsplat integration point, and a footprint plausible on a free T4 -- but disclose in the Orbit Studio README that Difix's checkpoints/code are under NVIDIA's non-commercial research-and-evaluation license (plus a Stability AI community license for a sub-component), so redistribution of trained artifacts should stay non-commercial.

Do not vendor GVCLab/GSFixer or GSFix3D into the pipeline yet. GSFixer's GitHub repo has no LICENSE file at all (GitHub API reports license:null, i.e. default all-rights-reserved) and its backbone is a 5B-parameter CogVideoX-5B-I2V video-diffusion model run for 50 denoising steps, trained on 8x H20/H100 -- far outside a free T4's 16GB. GSFix3D additionally requires a per-scene diffusion fine-tuning step, inherits the non-commercial Gaussian-Splatting-License plus a RAIL++-M model license, and was only validated on a 24GB RTX 4500 Ada.

Watch GaMO (github.com/yichuanH/GaMO_official, CC BY 4.0, code already public) as the conceptually closest fit for 'filling gaps between a handful of outdoor viewpoints' -- it reframes sparse-view reconstruction as FOV-expansion/outpainting on top of a DUSt3R+3DGS coarse init and runs in ~8 min/scene on a single RTX 4090 (25x faster than the GuidedVD-3DGS diffusion baseline it beats). It is not yet ready to integrate: the repo still needs 3 separate conda environments (unification was only 'planned for Feb 2026'), ships only an indoor Replica demo, and publishes no outdoor/panorama example or baseline-PSNR-delta table.

Track but do not build against VidSplat (CC BY 4.0, training-free, adapts pretrained Wan2.1 I2V) and OracleGS (WACV 2026, propose-and-validate MVS-oracle for filtering diffusion hallucinations) -- both target exactly this sparse-outdoor-capture problem and both have permissive-or-unstated licensing, but neither has a confirmed, working public code/checkpoint release as of 2026-07-23 (VidSplat is a ~2-month-old project-page-only preprint; no GitHub repo was found for OracleGS at all). Re-check in a few months.

Structural note: since Orbit Studio already reframes equirectangular frames into perspective crops before COLMAP/gsplat, any of these repair models would plug in downstream on those perspective renders -- no change needed to the equirect-to-perspective step. But none of the six papers evaluate on true 360/equirect panorama captures; all report PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on pinhole 3-9-view splits (DL3DV, Mip-NeRF 360, Replica, ScanNet++). Treat any expected PSNR gain as unverified for the 20-still-panorama bridge scenario until tested on the project's own captures.
slice: Diffusion/video-prior artifact repair and view densification for sparse-view 3DGS (Difix3D+, GSFixer, GSFix3D, VidSplat, OracleGS, GaMO)
summary:
A 'generative repair' cluster for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting has consolidated over the last year, all sharing one mechanism: a diffusion or video-diffusion model synthesizes/cleans novel-view 2D images, which are fed back as extra photometric supervision into standard 3DGS optimization -- meaning every method is a data-augmentation front-end, not a change to the splat trainer itself, so any of them can in principle sit in front of gsplat or Brush unmodified. Maturity and licensing vary sharply. NVIDIA Difix3D+ (CVPR 2025 Oral) is the most usable today: public HuggingFace weights (nvidia/difix, nvidia/difix_ref), a single-step SD-Turbo-scale model (cheap versus the rest), and a documented nerfstudio/gsplat post-processing hook -- but under NVIDIA's non-commercial research license plus a Stability AI sub-license. GSFixer (ICML 2026, GVCLab) and GSFix3D (arXiv 2508.14717) post the strongest artifact-restoration numbers (GSFixer beats Difix3D+ and GenFusion on the new DL3DV-Res benchmark) but need a 5B-parameter CogVideoX-5B video-diffusion backbone trained on H20/H100 clusters (GSFixer) or per-scene diffusion fine-tuning on a 24GB Ada card (GSFix3D) -- neither fits a free T4, and GSFixer ships no LICENSE file at all. GaMO (arXiv 2512.25073, CC BY 4.0, code public) reframes the problem as geometry-aware outpainting and is the best conceptual match for filling gaps between few outdoor viewpoints, running in ~8 min/scene on an RTX 4090, but its repo is still pre-alpha (3 conda envs, indoor-only demo). VidSplat (arXiv 2605.11424, CC BY 4.0, training-free, built on Wan2.1) and OracleGS (arXiv 2509.23258, WACV 2026, MVS-oracle-validated generation) are promising on paper but have no confirmed working public code release yet.</summary>

key_claims: Difix is used as 'the final post-processing step at render time', compatible with nerfstudio and gsplat pipelines

Licensed under a custom NVIDIA License (non-commercial, research/evaluation only) plus a Stability AI Community License component; GitHub reports license as 'Other/NOASSERTION'

used or intended for use non-commercially

sources.title: GSFixer: Improving 3D Gaussian Splatting with Reference-Guided Video Diffusion Priors (ICML 2026)
key_claims: Uses a DiT-based video diffusion model (CogVideoX-5b-I2V) fine-tuned on 1,000 DL3DV-10K scenes with 8x NVIDIA H20 GPUs for ~4 days
Requires 50 denoising steps at inference, noted by authors as an efficiency limitation
On the new DL3DV-Res benchmark: PSNR 16.72 vs GenFusion 14.56 and Difix3D+ 14.14
GitHub API reports license: null -- no LICENSE file present in the repository
Weights hosted at huggingface.co/flow666/GSFixer; benchmark dataset huggingface.co/datasets/flow666/DL3DV-Res_Benchmark

sources.title: GSFix3D: Diffusion-Guided Repair of Novel Views in Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: Authors: Jiaxin Wei, Stefan Leutenegger, Simon Schaefer
Combines a fine-tuned latent diffusion model (also called 'GSFixer' in this paper, distinct from the GVCLab ICML repo) with random mask augmentation for inpainting
Code repo (GSFix3D/GSFix3D) tested on Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, NVIDIA RTX 4500 Ada (24GB-class)
Requires per-scene fine-tuning of the diffusion model before inference
License stack: Gaussian-Splatting-License (non-commercial) + Apache 2.0 for parts of the codebase + RAIL++-M License for models
quotes: Our code and data will be made publicly available

sources.title: VidSplat: Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction with Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion Priors
key_claims: Training-free framework built on pretrained Wan2.1 I2V video diffusion, no per-scene fine-tuning required
Uses visibility-based camera pose sampling plus stage-wise denoising to keep generated views 3D-consistent
DL3DV novel-view synthesis at 6 views: outdoor PSNR 17.49, SSIM 0.561, LPIPS 0.376
Paper licensed CC BY 4.0; project page at tangjm24.github.io/VidSplat, no confirmed populated GitHub code repo found

sources.title: OracleGS: Grounding Generative Priors for Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: Authors: Atakan Topaloglu, Kunyi Li, Michael Niemeyer, Nassir Navab, A. Murat Tekalp, Federico Tombari; accepted WACV 2026
Uses a 'propose-and-validate' strategy: a 3D-aware diffusion model proposes novel views, a repurposed multi-view-stereo model acts as an 'oracle' producing uncertainty maps that weight the 3DGS loss
Evaluated on Mip-NeRF 360 and NeRF Synthetic; no GitHub code repository was found in searches
quotes: Regressive models are geometrically faithful but incomplete, whereas generative models can complete scenes but often introduce structural inconsistencies

sources.title: GaMO: Geometry-aware Multi-view Diffusion Outpainting for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction
key_claims: Authors from National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (Yi-Chuan Huang et al., incl. Yu-Lun Liu)
Reframes sparse-view reconstruction as FOV-expansion/outpainting on a DUSt3R + 3DGS coarse initialization, using the MVGenMaster diffusion backbone with opacity masks and Plucker ray embeddings
Runs in ~8 minutes/scene on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090, a claimed 25x speedup over the GuidedVD-3DGS diffusion baseline (3+ hours)
Mip-NeRF 360 outdoor sparse-view results: 6-view PSNR 16.74/SSIM 0.393/LPIPS 0.436; 9-view PSNR 17.56/SSIM 0.448/LPIPS 0.381

Paper licensed CC BY 4.0; code public at github.com/yichuanH/GaMO_official but requires 3 separate conda environments and a hard DUSt3R ViT-Large checkpoint dependency; only an indoor Replica demo is documented
quotes: expands the field of view (FOV) to cover unobserved regions while preserving geometric consistency

sources.title: GSFixer (arXiv abstract/HTML)
key_claims: Introduces DL3DV-Res, a new benchmark of artifact frames rendered from low-quality 3DGS reconstructions
Integrates 2D semantic features (DINOv2) and 3D geometric features (VGGT) of reference views to guide video diffusion restoration
